before.best_for: Character-consistent AI image editing across multiple third-party models, AI influencer and social content creation
before.description: Nano Banana (nanobanana.io) is an independent AI image editing platform, not affiliated with Google, that offers character-consistent photo edits by routing requests to several third-party image and video models.
before.description_long:
Nano Banana, at nanobanana.io, is an independent AI image generation and editing platform. Despite sharing its name with Google's own Nano Banana image models, the site states on its own pages that it has no affiliation with Google or any other product it references. It functions as a multi-model service, giving users access to several third-party models — including Seedream, GPT Image, Veo, Sora, Kling, Seedance and Qwen — through a single interface, rather than running a single proprietary model.

The platform is live and operating. Its core workflow is in-context editing: you upload a photo, describe the change in plain language, and the service applies the edit while aiming to preserve the original composition, lighting and scene structure, rather than generating an image from scratch.

Its headline feature is character consistency — keeping the same face, outfit or object recognizable across multiple edits or scenes, which the site markets toward serialized content creators, AI-influencer accounts and branded campaigns. Higher paid tiers add API access and support for multiple seats, aimed at teams rather than solo use.

Pricing is organized into Basic, Pro and Enterprise tiers, each billed annually, with credit allowances that scale with tier (roughly 15,000 credits/year on Basic up to 120,000 credits/year on Enterprise). The site also lists monthly and one-time purchase options, but those figures were not independently verified. New users receive a batch of free sign-in credits of unstated size before any purchase is required.

Because nanobanana.io is a reseller of outside models rather than Google's own Nano Banana (Gemini image models, available via the Gemini app, Google AI Studio and the Gemini API), its output quality and feature set depend on whichever underlying model it routes a given request to, and those models can change independent of this card. It suits creators who want a single interface for character-consistent editing without committing to one model vendor, but users who specifically want Google's Gemini image models should go directly to Google's own products.
pros: Markets strong character consistency for repeated edits of the same face, outfit or object
In-context editing aims to preserve original lighting, perspective and composition
Single interface gives access to multiple third-party image and video models (Seedream, GPT Image, Veo, Sora, Kling, Seedance, Qwen, others)
Free credits granted on sign-in before any payment
Pro and Enterprise tiers add API access and multi-seat support for teams
cons: Not affiliated with Google despite sharing the Nano Banana name, which risks confusion with Google's actual Gemini image models
Published lower rates (e.g. the discounted Basic tier) are annual-billing prices, not monthly billing
Amount of free sign-in credits is not disclosed, so real usage limits are unclear upfront
Monthly and one-time pricing options are mentioned but not detailed on the pricing page
Output quality depends on whichever third-party model handles a given request, which can change over time
choose_if: ✅ You create AI influencer content and need consistent character generation across many images
✅ You want AI image editing with precise control over specific characters
✅ You're a content creator needing a consistent virtual persona for social media
✅ You want a single interface to access several third-party image/video models rather than one dedicated model

faq.a: Nano Banana at nanobanana.io is an independent AI image editing platform, not affiliated with Google, that specializes in character consistency — keeping the same face, outfit or object recognizable across multiple edited images. It works by routing edits to several third-party image and video models rather than running a single proprietary model.

There is no ongoing free plan. New users receive a batch of free credits on sign-in (amount not disclosed) to try the editing features, and continued or heavier use requires one of the paid Basic, Pro or Enterprise tiers, which are billed annually.

after.best_for: AI image generation and editing within Google's Gemini ecosystem, including multi-turn character-consistent edits and studio-quality output
after.description: Nano Banana is Google's family of Gemini image generation and editing models, including Nano Banana 2, Nano Banana 2 Lite, Nano Banana 2.1 and Nano Banana Pro, available through the Gemini app, Google AI Studio and the Gemini API.
after.description_long:
Nano Banana is Google's family of state-of-the-art image generation and editing models, built on Gemini. It is developed and operated by Google itself, distinct from unaffiliated third-party websites that borrow the Nano Banana name.

The current family comprises Nano Banana 2.1 (gemini-nano-banana-2.1, an update to Nano Banana 2), Nano Banana 2 (Gemini 3.1 Flash Image), Nano Banana 2 Lite (Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite Image), and Nano Banana Pro (Gemini 3 Pro Image). The original Nano Banana model (Gemini 2.5 Flash Image) was deprecated in the API and shut down on October 2, 2026.

The models accept image and text input and let users refine results conversationally in plain language. Capabilities include multi-turn character consistency, accurate text rendering, and search-grounded generation drawing on Gemini's real-world knowledge, with output resolutions up to 4K. Nano Banana Pro targets studio-quality precision and control, Nano Banana 2 offers pro-level generation and editing at Flash speed, and Nano Banana 2 Lite is the fastest, most efficient model in the family. The models are accessible through the Gemini app's Create images tool, Google AI Studio, and the Gemini API. All generated images carry an invisible SynthID watermark, and images made in the Gemini app also carry a visible watermark.

In the Gemini app, Nano Banana 2 is free to use, while Nano Banana 2.1 requires a paid Google AI plan (AI Plus, AI Pro or AI Ultra); paid plans also unlock higher generation limits and the ability to redo an image with Nano Banana Pro. No numeric usage limits are published for free use. The Gemini API has no free tier for these models and bills per output image on its paid tier: Nano Banana 2.1 costs about $0.034 at 1K resolution, $0.050 at 2K and $0.113 at 4K; Nano Banana 2 costs about $0.045 at 0.5K, $0.067 at 1K, $0.101 at 2K and $0.151 at 4K; Nano Banana 2 Lite costs about $0.034 at 1K; and Nano Banana Pro costs about $0.134 at 1K/2K and $0.24 at 4K. Batch processing is available at half price.

Limitations include the lack of published numeric limits for free app use, a visible watermark on Gemini app images, no free tier on the API, and a 4K cap on output resolution.

Nano Banana suits casual users who want free in-app image editing, developers who need API access to Google's latest image models, and teams wanting studio-quality editing with character consistency; those needing unlimited free API access should look elsewhere.

The Gemini API has no free tier; every output image is billed per generation
